summaries.gardner: Corning shows several Rule Breaker traits: it leads in optical fiber for the fast-growing AI data-center build-out, has a top-tier partner (Nvidia's 2026 investment), and commentators often call the stock expensive. It is less of a fit on being a young, emerging-industry leader with a famous consumer brand, because it is a 175-year-old company whose display, auto and life-sciences businesses are mature.
summaries.buffett: Corning has durable know-how and long customer relationships, but its record is uneven (a GAAP loss in 2017, revenue flat from 2021 to 2024), it is capital-intensive, and debt of $8.4B exceeds cash of $2.5B. At about 61 times trailing GAAP earnings it also lacks the reasonable price Buffett wants.
summaries.munger: Munger would value Corning's hard-to-copy process know-how in fiber and specialty glass and its long-serving management. Inverting, the risks are cyclical display and solar businesses, Chinese competition, AI-spending swings and heavy capital needs, and the current multiple leaves little room for error.
summaries.lynch: Corning fits Lynch's 'stalwart turned fast grower' category: core EPS rose 29% in 2025 and 30% in Q2 2026 on AI fiber demand, a simple story he would like. But the stock is widely followed rather than overlooked, the share count has risen, and a forward P/E of about 40 is above its roughly 30% EPS growth.
summaries.fisher: Corning matches many of Fisher's points: steady R&D ($1.11B of RD&E in 2025) that produces new products from Gorilla Glass to photonics, products with room to grow, and a long-tenured management team. Profit margins are only mid-teens and have been volatile, which is weaker against his 'worthwhile profit margin' test.
summaries.graham: Corning fails most of Graham's defensive tests: it had a GAAP loss in 2017, has paid dividends only since 2007, and trades at about 61 times trailing earnings and about 9 times book value. Its size and current ratio of 1.8 are its only clear passes.
summaries.thiel: Corning has real proprietary process technology and a strong sales channel to hyperscalers, and the timing for AI fiber looks right. But it does not have a 10x technology lead or a monopoly in most of its markets, where AGC, NEG, Prysmian, Fujikura and Chinese makers compete.
summaries.gerstner: Gerstner would see Corning as a beneficiary of the AI infrastructure build-out, with accelerating earnings (Q3 2026 guidance of about +28% core EPS) and big customer contracts with Meta, Amazon and Nvidia. Valuation discipline is the problem: free-cash-flow yield is about 2% and a $2B at-the-market share program shows capital needs.
summaries.druckenmiller: Earnings are accelerating and 2027 EPS estimates rose through 2026, which fits Druckenmiller's focus on improving fundamentals and catalysts such as new hyperscaler deals. The stock's 51% fall from its June 2026 high shows how crowded the AI trade became, so timing and liquidity matter more than usual.
summaries.smith: Terry Smith wants high returns on capital, high gross margins and low capital intensity; Corning's 36% GAAP gross margin, roughly 15% core ROIC and heavy capex make it a weaker fit. It also does not pass 'don't overpay' at about 47 times free cash flow.
summaries.greenblatt: On the Magic Formula Corning ranks poorly: trailing operating income of about $2.6B is only about 2% of its roughly $120B enterprise value. Its return on capital is respectable but not exceptional for a capital-heavy manufacturer.
summaries.akre: Corning partly meets Akre's three-legged stool: a good business with real moats in fiber and specialty glass, and capable long-serving managers. Its ability to reinvest at high returns has improved with customer-funded capacity, but historic returns were modest and dilution is rising.
summaries.pabrai: Corning is not a Dhandho-style bet: it is a well-known, fully priced AI winner, not a simple, distressed business at a deep discount. The chance of permanent business loss is low, but the chance of a lasting loss from overpaying is meaningful.
summaries.wood: Corning supplies the fiber and photonics behind AI computing, which ties it to ARK's AI platform, and it is expanding into solar materials. But it is an established materials maker, not a pure disruptive-innovation leader with falling cost curves, and its addressable market is unlikely to grow many times in five years.
summaries.ackman: Ackman looks for simple, predictable, free-cash-flow-generative businesses with strong balance sheets and moats; Corning has the moat, but its results are cyclical, debt exceeds cash and free-cash-flow margin is about 14%. The price also gives little of the discount to intrinsic value he wants.
summaries.sleep: Corning partly fits Nick Sleep's 'scale economics shared': its customer co-investment model lets it build US fiber capacity that rivals struggle to match. But it does not obviously hand scale savings back to customers to deepen its moat, and its 10-20-year position is hard to forecast in cyclical glass markets.
summaries.valentine: Corning sells into a huge, painful problem (moving vast amounts of AI data with light) at the right time, which fits Valentine's market-first view. It is a mature public company, not a young company aiming at a new market, so the venture lens fits only partly.
summaries.nash: On Nash's process Corning passes the secular-trend, growth (about 18%) and profitability tests and scores about 85 of 130 on his categories, but it fails the instant-kill rules for more debt than cash and a GAAP operating margin of about 15%. His DCF and multiple checks also show the price well above the value implied by its historic growth and cash flow.

momentum.evidence: The stock is up about 52% over 52 weeks to $132.00 (16 Oct 2026), but it has fallen about 51% from its 30 June 2026 high of $271.78.

g4.evidence: CEO Wendell Weeks has led Corning since 2005, and Nvidia invested $500M for warrants in May 2026, alongside multiyear deals with Meta, Amazon and Apple.

g6.evidence: Bears have pointed to forward P/E of about 55x in May 2026 and NTM EV/EBITDA near 30x versus a peer median of about 19x, and the stock fell sharply on valuation worries in July and September 2026.

simple.evidence: The core businesses (fiber, display and cover glass, auto filters) are understandable, but five segments with yen hedges and large core-vs-GAAP adjustments make the numbers harder to follow.

b2.evidence: Results have been uneven: a GAAP net loss of $497M in 2017, revenue of $14,082M in 2021 falling to $12,588M in 2023, then rising to $15,629M in 2025.

integrity.evidence: Corning sets public targets and hit its Springboard 20% core operating-margin goal a year early, but it leans heavily on non-GAAP core results ($2,199M core vs $1,596M GAAP net income in 2025) and started a $2B at-the-market share sale in September 2026.

b6.evidence: Corning grows by organic capacity largely funded by customers (Apple, Meta, Amazon, Nvidia) rather than an acquisition spree.

roic.evidence: Corning's core ROIC was 14.9% in Q2 2026, up from 13.1%, and GAAP return on equity was about 14% in 2025, but returns were much lower in 2023-2024 (net income $581M and $506M).

fcf.evidence: Free cash flow (operating cash flow minus capex) was $1,413M in 2025 versus $1,596M of net income, but heavy capex keeps FCF margins modest (about 9% in 2025).

b10.evidence: Corning pays out most of its earnings ($971M of dividends in 2025) and reinvests heavily in capex; the recent AI fiber growth shows payoff, but revenue was flat for most of 2021-2024.

safety.evidence: At $132 the stock trades at about 61 times trailing GAAP EPS of $2.17 and about 47 times trailing free cash flow, with no conservative margin of safety.

fairprice.evidence: A forward P/E of about 40 on 2026 core EPS consensus of $3.29 is high, though core EPS is growing about 30% and the stock has already fallen about half from its peak.

mu5.evidence: Corning is unlikely to fail outright, but it could be hurt by an AI capex slowdown, Chinese glass and fiber capacity, solar policy changes and yen swings.

reinvest.evidence: Customer-funded capacity for Meta, Amazon and Nvidia lets it reinvest at about 15% core ROIC with years of AI demand ahead, though display and solar earn lower returns.

ly2.evidence: It is a stalwart turned fast grower: AI fiber demand lifted Optical Communications sales 35% in 2025, with the Springboard plan targeting a $30B run rate by end-2028.

ly3.evidence: The forward P/E of about 40 is above expected 2026 core EPS growth of about 31% ($2.52 to $3.29), and trailing GAAP P/E is about 61.

runway.evidence: Management targets $40B of annualized sales by end-2030, up from $16.4B of core sales in 2025, from AI fiber, US solar and photonics.

ly7.evidence: Diluted shares rose from 772M (2020) to 875M (Q2 2026), with a $2B ATM equity program and Nvidia warrants for up to 15M shares.

ly8.evidence: Corning is a crowded, widely covered AI trade with 18 analysts setting price targets and 74% institutional ownership.

fi2.evidence: As display glass matured, Corning built Gorilla Glass, AI-data-center connectivity, US solar wafers and a photonics platform launched in May 2026.

fi3.evidence: R&D produced new growth lines; Optical Communications sales grew from $4,657M in 2024 to $6,274M in 2025 on new high-density fiber and connectivity products.

fi4.evidence: It wins very large, multiyear contracts with leaders (Meta up to $6B, Amazon, Nvidia, Apple $2.5B), though through engineering partnerships more than a sales machine.

longterm.evidence: Corning kept RD&E spending above $1B a year through the 2023 downturn ($1,076M in 2023, $1,110M in 2025).

gr1.evidence: Corning is a $114B market-cap company with $15.6B of 2025 sales, founded in 1851.

ni10.evidence: Corning reported a GAAP net loss of $497M in 2017 because of US tax reform.

gr4.evidence: Corning has paid a quarterly dividend since restarting it at $0.05 in September 2007, about 19 years, just short of Graham's 20.

eps10.evidence: 2025 diluted EPS was $1.83, below 2016's one-off $3.23 but well above the -$0.66 of 2017, so the 10-year comparison depends on the base year.

gr6.evidence: The price is about 128 times average GAAP diluted EPS of $1.03 for 2023-2025 ($0.68, $0.58, $1.83).

gr7.evidence: With P/E of about 61 and price-to-book of about 9, the product is about 550, far above 22.5.

th1.evidence: Corning's fiber and glass are better but not ten times better than offerings from Prysmian, Fujikura, AGC or NEG.

timing.evidence: AI data centers need far more fiber per rack, and Corning's Optical Communications sales grew 32% in Q2 2026 with Enterprise Networks up 65%.

th3.evidence: Corning built leadership in niche markets (low-loss fiber, LCD glass, cover glass) and expanded from there, but it is now a large incumbent, not a startup.

team.evidence: Weeks has 21 years as CEO and delivered the Springboard plan early, but this is a strong professional team rather than an exceptional founder.

th5.evidence: Corning sells directly to hyperscalers, carriers, Apple, Samsung and panel makers under multiyear agreements.

durable.evidence: Fiber and specialty glass should remain essential for decades, but Chinese competitors and possible shifts in AI interconnect designs could erode Corning's position.

th7.evidence: Its customer co-funded US manufacturing model and early bet on AI data-center fiber were distinctive, but rivals now see the same opportunity.

trend.evidence: Corning is a leading supplier of optical fiber and connectivity for the AI build-out, with deals with Meta, Amazon and Nvidia.

dr1.evidence: Core EPS grew 26% in Q4 2025 and 30% in Q2 2026, Q3 guidance calls for about +28%, and 2027 EPS consensus rose 9% in the three months to July 2026.

dr2.evidence: New Nvidia and Amazon capacity and Solar profitability expected to improve from Q3 2026 should help, but much of this is already in management's public targets.

dr4.evidence: AI capex spending is a strong tailwind, but Corning carries $8.4B of debt and its display, auto and solar businesses are sensitive to the economy, the yen and trade policy.

dr6.evidence: Catalysts include ramps of the Nvidia (May 2026) and Amazon (June 2026) agreements, Springboard plan updates and quarterly results.

gm.evidence: GAAP gross margin was 36.0% in 2025 and core gross margin 39.6% in Q2 2026: solid for a manufacturer, but not the 60%+ of top franchises.

fcfyield.evidence: Trailing free cash flow of about $2.40B on a market cap of about $114B is a yield of about 2.1%.

gb2.evidence: Trailing GAAP operating income of about $2.6B is only about 2.2% of an enterprise value of about $120B.

pa2.evidence: The stock has halved since June 2026 on valuation and dilution worries, but the business itself is growing about 17% and is not in a setback.

pa4.evidence: Business failure risk is low given its scale and customer contracts, but paying about 40 times forward earnings carries real risk of a lasting loss if AI demand slows.

ns4.evidence: AI fiber and US manufacturing could strengthen its position, but display share is eroding to Chinese makers.
